To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@amazon.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cloudreseller.com>
Cc: procurement@atlasanalytics.com
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: SKU slicing & regional packaging decisions for Atlas Analytics marketplace listings

Team / partners —

We need to lock the listing strategy for Atlas Analytics (DL-2027-119) by end of this week so Marketplace ops can start asset creation. Main decisions we still need:

- SKU granularity per cloud (single multi-arch SKU vs. per-instance-type SKUs)
- Region packaging: mirror Atlas' deployed regions (NA/EU/APAC) or staggered (NA first, then EU, APAC)
- Pricing packaging for co-sell eligibility on AWS (metered vs. subscription) — Sarah can you confirm constraints?

Attached is a draft SKU matrix and region priority doc (redwood_sku_slicing_v2.xlsx, atlas_region_priority_matrix.pdf). My recommendation is: one SKU per cloud with two offering tiers (Entry / Pro) to avoid listing sprawl, then use variants for region-specific pricing where required. But I want engineering and sales input on technical feasibility and GTM impact.

Can each of you reply with 1) feasibility notes, 2) blocker items, and 3) any mandatory partner requirements.

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SKU slicing & regional packaging decisions for Atlas Analytics marketplace listings

Eve — quick engineering read:

1) One SKU per cloud with two offering tiers (Entry / Pro) is the easiest to maintain from a runtime/packaging perspective. We can use image/instance-type compatibility flags for instance-specific requirements rather than creating separate SKUs per instance. That keeps the registry small and avoids a combinatorial explosion when we add quantized builds.

2) Region variants: technically trivial (Marketplace supports pricing variants per region), but there are tradeoffs:
   - If we create per-region SKUs, customers see explicit regional availability which reduces support friction but increases listing maintenance.
   - If we use a single SKU with region metadata, we must ensure our deployment routing and billing mapping are bulletproof. Failure modes show up in support tickets.

3) Blockers: access to Atlas' final region list and any data residency constraints (need the signed compliance addendum). Also need confirmation on whether Atlas requires dedicated VPC private listing (affects packaging and listing metadata).

I've added technical notes in redwood_sku_slicing_v2.xlsx (tab: engineering_notes).

—Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@amazon.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cloudreseller.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 11:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SKU slicing & regional packaging decisions for Atlas Analytics marketplace listings

Adding GTM/partnership perspective:

- Co-sell trigger: AWS requires a metered offer or a subscription with 12-month minimum for certain co-sell programs; Sarah can confirm the exact language. Our recommended approach for Atlas (mid-market customers) is subscription with monthly billing and an optional annual discount — that buys simpler procurement for Atlas while keeping co-sell eligibility via participation programs.

- Regional rollout: recommend NA first (90-day runway to iron out billing & support), then EU, then APAC. Atlas has a heavy EU presence so we could parallelize NA+EU if compliance checks finish early.

- SKUs: prefer single SKU per cloud with 2 tiers. Sales asks: ability to present usage-based addons (e.g., extra token quotas) as add-on SKUs or plans — important for expansion motions.

I'll coordinate with Atlas procurement (cc'd) on contract terms and run the commercial language through legal.

-Marissa
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@amazon.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cloudreseller.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SKU slicing & regional packaging decisions for Atlas Analytics marketplace listings

Thanks for the detail — AWS Marketplace ops here. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Co-sell eligibility: AWS prefers subscription offers for co-sell partner programs. Metered billing is supported but may delay co-sell onboarding because of additional measurement verification. For fastest path to co-sell we recommend a 12-month subscription with monthly invoice option (this still satisfies many co-sell programs).

- Regions & pricing: We allow regional price overrides; however, each regional override triggers separate compliance and tax checks. If you want a fast NA+EU launch, keep the same SKU and use regional pricing overrides only for EU (where VAT applies). Avoid per-instance SKUs for initial launch.

- Listings metadata: Please include clear VPC/private listing flags if Atlas requires private offers (this affects how we surface the product in the Marketplace UI).

Happy to set up a short ops call if you want to walk through the listing creation checklist.

—Sarah
AWS Marketplace Partner Ops
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SKU slicing & regional packaging decisions for Atlas Analytics marketplace listings

Operational notes from pricing/cost perspective:

- Two tiers (Entry / Pro) map well to our autoscaling & instance family support. Entry: small models, limited KV cache; Pro: larger KV cache + priority throughput. We should publish expected latency/throughput per tier in the listing to set SLAs expectations.

- Metering for add-ons (token packs) is doable but needs us to instrument token accounting in the billing path. That adds ~3 weeks to the initial launch if we want it in the first release. My recommendation: launch without metered addons, enable them in a follow-on release (Post-launch +6 weeks).

- Attachment: I added a cost sensitivity tab in redwood_sku_slicing_v2.xlsx with per-region cost delta assumptions.

-Ben
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@amazon.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cloudreseller.com>, procurement@atlasanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SKU slicing & regional packaging decisions for Atlas Analytics marketplace listings — Final decisions & next steps

Thanks all for the quick turn. Summary of decisions (locked):

1) SKU model: one SKU per cloud (AWS / Azure / GCP) with two offering tiers (Entry / Pro). We will NOT create per-instance SKUs for launch.

2) Pricing & co-sell: primary offer will be a 12-month subscription (monthly invoicing option) to satisfy co-sell onboarding paths on AWS. We will surface optional metered addons in a follow-on release (target +6 weeks).

3) Regions: NA + EU initial launch (parallel). APAC will follow once compliance/canary telemetry looks healthy. Atlas procurement — please confirm the EU data residency addendum by EOD Mon (I've attached atlas_region_priority_matrix.pdf).

4) Technical: Karthik & team to prepare the variant metadata (region price override for EU) and VPC/private listing flags if Atlas requires them. Ben will bake the expected latency/throughput tables into the listing copy.

5) Ops: Sarah — please schedule a 30-min listing checklist call early next week (we prefer Tue/Wed).

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Karthik: finalize listing artifacts & engineering_notes in redwood_sku_slicing_v2.xlsx (due Mon 2027-05-31)
- Marissa: finalize commercial terms with Atlas legal (due Mon 2027-05-31)
- Ben: add cost sensitivity and publish performance table for listing (due Wed 2027-06-02)
- Sarah: listing ops call invite (due Mon 2027-05-31)

Attachments: redwood_sku_slicing_v2.xlsx (with engineering_notes & cost_sensitivity tabs), atlas_region_priority_matrix.pdf, co-sell_requirements_aws.md

If no objections by EOD Monday, we'll kick creative and listings operations on Tuesday.

Evelyn
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
